chunks: ‘Abdullah ibn Ibrahim ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Ja‘far ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Salit al-Zaydi, Abu al-Hakam said; and ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Umarah al-Jarmi informed me, from Yazid ibn Salit, who said:

I met Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) while we were intending to perform ‘Umrah, at a place along the road. I said: “May I be made your ransom, do you recognize this place where we are?” He said: “Yes; do you recognize it too?” I said: “Yes. My father and I met you here while you were with Abū ‘Abdillāh (عليه السلام), and your brothers were with him. My father said to him: ‘May my father and mother be your ransom, all of you are purified Imams, and no one is free from death. So tell me something which I may relate to the one who will succeed me after me, so that he may not go astray.’”

He said: “Yes, O Abū ‘Abdillāh, these are my children, and this one is their master,” and he pointed to you. “He has been taught judgment, understanding, generosity, and knowledge of what people need and of what they differ about in the affairs of their religion and their worldly life. In him are good character and good response, and he is a gate from the gates of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and in him is another quality better than all of that.” My father said to him: “What is it? May my father and mother be your ransom.” He (عليه السلام) said: “Allah, Mighty and Majestic, shall bring forth from him the relief of this Ummah, its succor, its banner, its light, its excellence, and its wisdom. He is the best newborn and the best youth. Through him Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will spare bloodshed, reconcile estrangement, gather what is scattered, mend what is split, clothe the naked, feed the hungry, give security to the fearful, send down rain, and show mercy to the servants. He is the best mature man and the best youth. His speech is judgment and his silence is knowledge. He clarifies for the people that wherein they differ, and he will lead his clan before the time of his maturity.” My father said to him: “May my father and mother be your ransom, has he been born?” He said: “Yes, and years have passed over him.”

Yazīd said: Then someone came to us such that we could not speak in his presence. Yazīd said: So I said to Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام): “Then you inform me with the like of what your father (عليه السلام) informed me.” He said to me: “Yes. My father (عليه السلام) was in a time that was not this time.” I said to him: “So whoever among you is satisfied with only this, then upon him be the curse of Allah.” He said: Abū Ibrāhīm laughed intensely, then said: “I shall inform you, O Abū ‘Umārah.”

“I left my house and made an outward وصية to one of my sons, and I associated my other sons with him in the outward matter; but inwardly I made the bequest to him alone and singled him out. Had the matter been left to me, I would have placed it in al-Qāsim my son because of my love for him and my compassion toward him; but that belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who places it where He wills. The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) came to me with news of him, then showed him to me and showed me those who would be with him. Thus none of us is designated until the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and my grandfather ‘Alī, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, come with the news of him. And I saw with the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) a ring, a sword, a staff, a book, and a turban.”

I said: “What are these, O Messenger of Allah?” He said to me: “As for the turban, it is the authority of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; as for the sword, it is the might of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; as for the book, it is the light of Allah, Blessed and Exalted; as for the staff, it is the power of Allah; and as for the ring, it gathers all these matters.” Then he said to me: “The command has gone from you to another than you.” I said: “O Messenger of Allah, show him to me; which one of them is he?” The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: “I have not seen among the Imams anyone more distressed at the separation from this command than you. Had the Imamate been by love, Ismā‘īl would have been more beloved to your father than you; but that is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

Then Abū Ibrāhīm said: “I saw all my children, the living among them and the dead. Amīr al-Mu’minīn (عليه السلام) said to me: ‘This one is their master,’ and he pointed to my son ‘Alī. ‘So he is from me and I am from him, and Allah is with the doers of good.’” Yazīd said: Then Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) said: “O Yazīd, this is a trust with you, so do not inform anyone of it except one who is intelligent or a servant whom you know to be truthful; and if you are asked about the testimony, then testify to it.”
And it is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Indeed Allah commands you to deliver trusts to their أهل.”
And He also said to us: “And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony he has from Allah?”

He said: Then Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) said: “So I turned to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and said: ‘You have gathered them for me; may my father and mother be your ransom, so which one of them is he?’ He said: ‘He is the one who sees by the light of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, hears with understanding, and speaks with wisdom. He is correct and does not err; he knows and is not ignorant, taught judgment and knowledge. He is this one,’ and he took the hand of my son ‘Alī.”

Then he said: “How little your stay with him will be. When you return from your journey, then make your وصية, set your affair in order, and finish what you intend, for you will be departing from them and dwelling with others than them. When you wish, call ‘Alī, and let him wash you and shroud you, for that is purity for you, and nothing is proper except that; and that is a sunnah that has already passed. Then lie down before him, arrange his brothers and his paternal uncles behind him, and command him to pronounce nine takbīrs over you. Thus his designation and authority over you will have been established while you are still alive. Then gather your children for him after them, make them witness against it, and call Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as witness; and Allah suffices as a witness.”

Yazīd said: Then Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) said to me: “I shall be seized in this year, and the command belongs to my son ‘Alī, the namesake of ‘Alī and ‘Alī. As for the first ‘Alī, he is ‘Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib; and as for the latter, he is ‘Alī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام). He has been given the understanding of the first, his forbearance, his support, his affection, his religion, and his trial; and the trial of the latter and his patience over what he dislikes. He is not to speak except four years after the death of Hārūn.”

Then he said to me: “O Yazīd, when you pass by this place and meet him—and you shall meet him—then give him glad tidings that there will be born to him a trustworthy, secure, blessed boy. He will inform you that you have indeed met me. At that time tell him that the slave-woman from whom this boy will be is a slave-woman from the household of Māriyah, the slave-woman of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), the mother of Ibrāhīm. If you are able to convey my salām to her, then do so.”

Yazīd said: After the passing of Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام), I met ‘Alī (عليه السلام), and he initiated me, saying: “O Yazīd, what do you say regarding ‘Umrah?” I said: “May my father and mother be your ransom, that is up to you, and I do not have the expenses.” He said: “Glory be to Allah! Were we ever to burden you and not suffice you?” So we went out until we came to that place. He initiated me and said: “O Yazīd, this is a place where you have often met your neighbors and your paternal uncles.” I said: “Yes.” Then I related the report to him, and he said to me: “As for the slave-woman, she has not yet arrived. When she comes, I will convey to her his salām.” We then went on to Makkah, and he purchased her in that year. She did not remain long before conceiving and giving birth to that boy.

Yazīd said: The brothers of ‘Alī had hoped to inherit from him, so his brothers showed hostility to me without any wrongdoing on my part. Then Isḥāq ibn Ja‘far said to them: “By Allah, I have seen him, and he indeed used to sit with Abū Ibrāhīm in the place in which I myself would not sit.”

key_terms.أَئِمَّةٌ: divinely designated Imams who lead the community
key_terms.الشَّهَادَةِ: testimony that must be upheld truthfully
key_terms.الْأَمَانَاتِ: trusts that must be returned to their rightful people
key_terms.الْأَمْرُ: the command or authority of the Imamate
key_terms.بَابٌ مِنْ أَبْوَابِ اللَّهِ: a divinely appointed means through which guidance is accessed
key_terms.وَدِيعَةٌ: a trust entrusted for preservation and proper delivery

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the designation of Imam al-Rida (عليه السلام) and the transmission of the Imamate?
ai.summary: This hadith is a detailed narrative of explicit indications toward the Imamate of Imam al-Rida (عليه السلام), conveyed through Yazid ibn Salit from Imam al-Kazim (عليه السلام) and earlier from Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام). It describes the divinely designated nature of the Imamate, the transmission of authority through the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and instructions regarding testimony, trust, and succession among the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام).
